sources.title: SteamDB - IOSoccer Dedicated Server (App 673990), type Tool, Source Engine, parent app IOSoccer 673560
IOSoccer: Dedicated Server Guide - srcds -game iosoccer -port 27015, rcon_password in cfg/server.cfg
AlliedModders Wiki - Setting up a Source Dedicated Server (Windows): SteamCMD install and srcds launch flags (-console, -game, +map) ONLY; this page documents no admin/RCON commands
Setting up a Source dedicated server on Linux - rcon kickid [number], rcon banid [x] [y] kick, rcon removeid [p], rcon writeid, rcon say [text], rcon stats
Source engine RCON admin commands - kick "<name>", kickid <userid> "<reason>", banid <minutes> <steamid>, removeid <steamid>, writeid, status
IOSoccer Admin Commands (hosting knowledge base) - rcon status, rcon kick <userid>, rcon banid <minutes> <userid>, rcon removeid <steamid>, rcon writeid, banned_user.cfg, rcon say
IOSoccer: Console Commands Guide - game-specific sv_/mp_ commands (sv_restart, sv_endmatch, sv_addplayercardban, sv_toggleplayeryellowcard); no kick or ban

Valve Developer Community - Console Command List: kick 'Kick a player by slot, userid or name', banid 'Add a user ID to the ban list.', removeid 'Remove a user ID from the ban list.', rcon_password, hostport 'Host game server port' (27015)

notes: IOSoccer is a stock Source dedicated server (srcds) launched with -game iosoccer; app 673990 is the 'IOSoccer Dedicated Server' tool (SteamDB: type Tool, Source Engine, parent app 673560), and LinuxGSM's iosserver module sets appid=673990, engine=source, '-game iosoccer ... -port 27015'. RCON is standard Valve Source RCON (TCP) on the server's own port, enabled by setting rcon_password in iosoccer/cfg/server.cfg; there is no separate RCON port or enable switch, and hostport is the Source cvar for that port (-port sets it). Confidence is LOW on purpose: every kick/ban/say string here is engine-level Source behaviour taken from GENERAL Source server documentation, not from any IOSoccer-specific official source - the developer's own material (iosoccer.com server manual, the published Console Commands guide) documents only match control (sv_restart, sv_endmatch, mp_*, sv_addplayercardban / sv_toggleplayeryellowcard / sv_removeplayercardban, which are in-match cards rather than moderation) and never mentions kick or ban. SOURCE CAVEAT: the AlliedModders wiki page cited is a SteamCMD/srcds setup guide and documents NO admin commands - it supports only the 'stock srcds' identity claim; the command strings rest on the two general Source write-ups (tjansson, GameServerKings) plus the IOSoccer hosting KB. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: the Legion Hosting knowledge base gives 'kick <userid>' and 'banid <minutes> <userid>', whereas the general Source documentation gives kick a NAME and kickid the userid; Valve's own Console Command List describes kick as 'Kick a player by slot, userid or name', so the hosting page is not necessarily wrong, but it is second-hand (it also lists mp_restartgame, which IOSoccer does not use) and is not treated as confirmation. kick is therefore templated on {playerName}, the form explicitly attested for Source; 'kickid <userid>' probably also works but no source confirms it for this build, and nothing confirms a Steam ID is accepted there. banid takes minutes (0 = permanent) and the Steam ID, with a trailing 'kick' to drop the player immediately. Bans exist only in memory until 'writeid' is run, which writes lines like 'banid 0 STEAM_0:1:12345678' to iosoccer/cfg/banned_user.cfg - the exact numeric formatting and whether the id is quoted vary by Source branch and were NOT verified for this build, so lineIdPattern is a best guess; IP bans are the separate addip/removeip/writeip list in iosoccer/cfg/banned_ip.cfg. Depending on the Source branch, status prints the id either as STEAM_0:1:12345678 or as [U:1:12345678]; both forms are accepted by the parse pattern. playerParse assumes the older single-column status format ('# <userid> "<name>" <uniqueid> ...'); newer Source branches print an extra leading index column and would not match, which is another reason for the low rating. There is no console command to set the MOTD - Source reads iosoccer/cfg/motd.txt - so motd is omitted.
